findings.reason: the followup is the dispatch driver, and both sections write the same two modules under the same store-doubling criterion, so either node can close on the other's measurement and the record of which section carries the work is lost.
findings.text: the driving followup `f-tfnsim-s28` says "§8 was discarded and rewritten … and has not been dispatched" and names only §8, while §14 states "§8 landed in part on 22 November 2026" and restates the same bound with new bases, so a coordinator acting on the followup dispatches a section whose remainder §14 has superseded

findings.reason: the section's own stated remaining driver is plan-set-sized and no arm can fail on it, so the node can close green while the deliverable's first clause is unmeasured.
findings.text: the done-when's only variations are the delivered-run store (eight vs forty entries; 12,266 vs 24,532 rows) and the test counts decoded rows for one node in a doubled store, while §14's body names "the roadmap's section-history read, which covers the project's whole plan set" as the remaining driver and the deliverable says the peak is "bounded by the plans and nodes the batch names" — nothing in the done-when grows the project's plan set with the batch's named nodes fixed, so a fix that narrows the run-store decode but still decodes every plan's history passes both arms and the test

findings.reason: the pass criterion is "at most half its peak at this section's base", so an unreconciled and unnamed base leaves the worker measuring half of a number the plan elsewhere contradicts.
findings.text: §14 quotes 14.16 GiB as its base eight-entry peak over 12,266 delivered-run rows, while the plan's own §8 record (plan.html:157) quotes 10.15 GiB as the base eight-entry peak over 58,836 rows with "the same instrument", and §14 names no base revision and does not say which revision produced the 11.75→22.19 GiB forty-entry pair
